results.evidence: dist_km (9.5 km = 5.9 mi) matches the approach text's own one-way trailhead-to-Sahale-Glacier-Camp figure, so it is a one-way number, not a third round-trip figure. The real disagreement is the itinerary total (5.7 + 9.2 = 14.9 mi) against the approach's ~16.8 mi round trip, which is the summit waypoint's distMi 8.4 doubled. One club route listing gives 14.0 mi / 5,500 ft for Horseshoe Peak via Sahale Arm, which is closer to the itinerary, but no second independent source with a round-trip figure could be fetched (several pages returned 403). Day 2 as scheduled (camp to summit and back, about 2.4 mi each way per the waypoints, then 5.7-6 mi out) would also run past 9.2 mi, so the itinerary may be low as well.

The contradiction is real inside the row: the schedule has the party back at camp at 1:00 PM after a 4:00 AM start (9 h), then a further 5.7 mi / 4,000 ft descent 'finishing by early evening', which cannot fit the 10 h that days[1].hours, timing.summitTimeHrs, sectionBreakdown[1].hrs and totalNote state. No source found gives timings for Sahale Glacier Camp to Horseshoe Peak and back, or for the day's total. Without that, it is not settled whether the hours or the schedule is wrong, so nothing was patched.

results.fact: Rope length for the crux pitch/rappel
results.evidence: rope_length_m 30 is the stated minimum, and descent_text, gear and rack all explain that 30 m is the minimum and that a 60 m rope gives margin. The fields describe one range consistently.

results.fact: Approach directions omit the current road closure stated elsewhere
results.evidence: The approach text describes the route from the trailhead and the road's surface. It never says the road is open to the trailhead. road.status, access.closures and itinerary.cal all carry the closure the same way, so no field on the page says the opposite. This is an omission in one section, not two fields that disagree.
dist_km is the one-way approach figure (it renders as 'Approach (one way)'). 12.1 km is 7.5 mi, and twice that is the approach text's ~15 mi round trip. The two fields agree.

The Lightning Creek / Willow Lake waypoints follow the route's own third approach_variant, which the row documents as a real alternative, and the Ross Dam trailhead waypoint note labels it as the long, historical approach. So a waypoint list for a non-primary approach is not by itself a false statement. What does not agree is inside the waypoints: distMi 11 and 15 against notes saying 'mile ~16' and '~mile 20'. A trail description confirms the East Bank trail leaves Ross Lake at about mile 16 to follow Lightning Creek, which backs the notes, but no second source fixes Willow Lake's mileage, and it is unclear which origin distMi counts from. The pins' positions are also out of scope, so nothing was patched.

Every route-specific field (face, overview, the summit waypoint at 8,003) puts this line on the South Peak, and high_point_ft 8071 is the North Peak's height. The encyclopedia entry for Hozomeen Mountain gives the South Peak as 8,003 ft (2,439 m). Two independent South Peak trip reports, one via Hozomeen Lake and one via the west gully, both give the summit as 8,003 ft. This is an alpine summit route, so the crag base-elevation convention does not apply.

dist_km 12.9 km is 8.0 mi one way, which implies about 16 mi round trip. That disagrees with the approach's ~19 km (about 12 mi) round trip and the itinerary's 12 mi. One South Peak report from the Hozomeen Lake trailhead gives 12 mi round trip. Another from the same campground, by a west-gully line, gives 15 mi. The two sources disagree, so the one-way figure is not settled.

results.fact: Total gain: gain_ft vs itinerary gain
results.evidence: gain_ft 6800 (loss_ft 6471) disagrees with the itinerary's own total of 6,300 ft gain (6,300 loss), with totalNote's 6,300, and with the approach's '6,400+'. One report from the Hozomeen Lake trailhead gives only its elevation range (1,720-8,003 ft). A west-gully report gives 7,500 ft gained and lost over a different line. Neither settles a figure for this route.

results.fact: Total elevation gain vs. loss for a car-to-car round trip
results.evidence: gain_ft 6266 is exactly the net difference of one report's elevation range (1,800-8,066 ft, 24.7 mi round trip from Skyline II), and loss_ft 545 is only the drop from camp to the saddle. Together they describe the ascent leg, not the car-to-car outing. The only round-trip total found is a single report of 24 mi and 9,600 ft gain, and no second source confirmed it. Because loss_ft holds two conventions in this catalog, it was not set equal to gain without a researched total.

dist_km is the one-way approach figure. 16.9 km is 10.5 mi, the approach's own one-way distance to the Monument 74 camp, and two independent reports put Monument 74 at mile 10.5 with about 24-25 mi round trip. Nothing on the row states a different one-way figure.
